comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the days to cover figure is doing a lot of work here and it is stale. that number is shares short over average daily volume, and your own post contains a 43.7M share day. once that lands in the average, 15.66 is not the number any more, it drops hard, and days to cover is most of the basis for calling this a squeeze setup at all.

borrow says the same thing. 5.42 percent with 400k available is an ordinary borrow, not a constrained one. when shorts are genuinely trapped the fee moves first and it moves a long way.

and short interest already down 9.2 percent is fuel spent rather than fuel waiting. that describes a position that largely covered into the move.

replies.author: Limp-Inevitable864
replies.body:
Fair criticism. The 15.66 DTC is backward-looking, and the 43.7M-share day will materially compress it once that volume enters the average. So I agree it shouldn’t be treated as the centerpiece of the setup.
Where I differ is that falling DTC doesn’t necessarily mean the remaining shorts covered. DTC has two moving pieces: short interest and average daily volume. Short interest was down 9.2%, so some bear harvest clearly occurred, but the denominator also exploded.
That’s why I’m interested in the next official short-interest print. If SI collapses, then you’re right: much of the squeeze fuel was spent. If a meaningful residual short position remains while CHPT continues holding the newly gained territory, then the falling DTC was largely a volume-compression effect rather than shorts escaping.
Same with borrow: 5.42% and 400K available is not distressed borrow, agreed. So I wouldn’t characterize the current setup as shorts being trapped by stock-loan conditions.
Good catch. I’d revise the current state to Bear Harvest Confirmed / Residual Short Book Unresolved and let the next SI report settle it. The data gets the last word.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: The next short interest print won't settle it in time either. It covers a settlement date about two weeks back and publishes days after that, so you'd be reading it well after the move it was meant to explain has already happened.

replies.author: Limp-Inevitable864
replies.body:
Agreed. The official SI print is too delayed to settle the live move. Better wording on my part: it can confirm afterward whether the residual short book actually contracted.

In real time I'm watching price acceptance, volume and borrow separately rather than assuming covering. 

CHPT is testing that distinction right now.

Battled back over 10.20

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: borrow is the one i'd trust most of those three. it moves the same day and the print never does. price acceptance over 10.20 into a close is what i'd want rather than the intraday tag.

replies.author: Limp-Inevitable864
replies.body:
That’s exactly the distinction. It’s not just an intraday tag anymore — CHPT pushed through 10.20 and accelerated to 10.40+. Now I want to see whether that territory is accepted into the close.
Borrow tells us what the bears are dealing with today. Price tells us whether they're actually losing territory. The later SI print can tell us afterward whether the short book contracted.
10.20 just became the interesting line.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: i'd write down what the close has to do before it gets there. 10.20 held into the bell means one thing, 10.20 given back in the last twenty minutes is the same chart with the opposite meaning, and it's far too easy to read it whichever way you were already leaning.

replies.author: Limp-Inevitable864
replies.body:
Agreed. Let’s freeze it now so we can’t reinterpret it at 4:00.
Close ≥ $10.20: reclaimed territory held.

Close < $10.20: reclaim failed today.
And I’ll keep the original LAND HO! levels intact too — LANDED was $10.01 and the published liberation test was $10.30–$10.45.
No moving the goalposts after the bell.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: writing the levels down before the bell is the only version of this worth anything. most people settle on what 10.20 meant after they've already seen where it closed.
